0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.
0040| #
0041| # Environment variables:
0042| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0043| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0044| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0045| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)
0046| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0047| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
0048| #   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
0049| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
0050| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
0051| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0052| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE        engine source the engine installer resolves against
0053| #                               (default: https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel)
0054| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER     the engine's own installer (default: forgel-install on PATH)
0055| #   FORGEL_ENGINE               engine binary whose version is read (default: forgel on PATH)
0056| #
0057| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.

0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.
0040| #
0041| # Environment variables:
0042| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0043| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0044| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0045| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)
0046| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0047| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
0048| #   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
0049| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
0050| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
0051| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0052| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE        engine source the engine installer resolves against
0053| #                               (default: https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel)
0054| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER     the engine's own installer (default: forgel-install on PATH)
0055| #   FORGEL_ENGINE               engine binary whose version is read (default: forgel on PATH)
0056| #
0057| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.
0058| 
0059| set -eu
0060| 
0061| # The exact markers an uninstall looks for. They are compared byte for byte.
0062| MARKER_START='# >>> forgel-code >>>'
0063| MARKER_END='# <<< forgel-code <<<'
0064| 
0065| # A profile whose last line has no final newline cannot be restored byte for
0066| # byte from the block alone: the newline that separates that line from the
0067| # block is indistinguishable from one the file always had. The installer
0068| # records the case in one comment line directly above the block and removes
0069| # that line, with the separator newline, together with the block.
0070| MARKER_SEPARATOR='# forgel-code: the line above had no final newline'
0071| 
0072| HOME_DIR=${HOME:-/}
0073| PREFIX=${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME_DIR/.local/share/forgel-code}
0074| BIN_DIR=${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME_DIR/.local/bin}
0075| LAUNCHER=$BIN_DIR/forgel-code
0076| TAG=${FORGEL_CODE_TAG:-v0.2.0}
0077| REPOSITORY=${FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY:-https://github.com/forgel-dev/code}
0078| 
0079| # The engine side of the installation: the source the run asks about, the
0080| # engine's own installer that answers and installs, and the binary whose version
0081| # report says what is already in place.
0082| ENGINE_SOURCE=${FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE:-https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel}
0083| ENGINE_INSTALLER=${FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER:-forgel-install}
0084| 
0085| # What the engine part of the run learned, filled in before anything is decided.
0086| # A failure report quotes whichever of them are known.
0087| ENGINE_MINIMUM=
0088| ENGINE_PRESENT=
0089| ENGINE_AVAILABLE=
0090| 
0091| # What a fresh shell reports back: its own PATH and the path it resolves
0092| # ``forgel-code`` to. The prefixes keep the answer readable next to anything a
0093| # system-wide profile may print.
0094| CHECK_PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
0095| CHECK_COMMAND='printf "forgel-fresh-path=%s\n" "$PATH"; fresh=$(command -v forgel-code || true); printf "forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\n" "$fresh"'
0096| 
0097| # The bound for the fresh-shell check, in seconds, when FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT is
0098| # unset, and the grace period the checked shell gets between the graceful stop
0099| # and the forceful one. A login shell reads its startup files in milliseconds;
0100| # ten seconds leaves room on a slow machine and still bounds a shell that never
0101| # answers.
0102| DEFAULT_VERIFY_LIMIT=10
0103| VERIFY_GRACE=2
0104| 
0105| # How long the installer waits for the watchdog's decision, in whole seconds,
0106| # derived from the grace period. One polling step of the watchdog is the longest
0107| # the decision can take after the checked command exits, so one grace period
0108| # covers it with room to spare. A watchdog that never answers cannot hold the
0109| # installer longer than this.
0110| DECISION_WAIT=$VERIFY_GRACE
0111| if [ "$DECISION_WAIT" -lt 1 ]; then
0112|     DECISION_WAIT=1
0113| fi
0114| 
0115| # The profile files this installer can have written. ``--uninstall`` cleans the
0116| # block out of every one of them, so no stale PATH entry stays behind. The list
0117| # is a superset of what the install path may edit, including ~/.bashrc, because

0060| ### The engine
0061| 
0062| The same run settles the engine the client runs. It first learns which engine
0063| version the configured engine source offers, without installing anything, and
0064| which version of an engine is already in place. Then it decides:
0065| 
0066| | Engine in place | Offered version | Result |
0067| | --- | --- | --- |
0068| | none | at or above the declared minimum | that version is installed |
0069| | at or above the minimum, and the offered version is not strictly newer | any | the engine is kept and nothing about it is changed |
0070| | below the offered version | supported and strictly newer | the strictly newer version replaces the engine in place |
0071| 
0072| A version equal to, or older than, the one in place is never installed. The
0073| engine versions are ordered numerically, component by component; one leading
0074| version prefix and trailing zero components do not change the comparison, and a
0075| version that cannot be ordered never counts as supported. The engine left in
0076| place always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version;
0077| when that cannot be reached the run ends as a failure instead of reporting the
0078| pair as installed: the offered version is below the minimum and no suitable
0079| engine is present, the engine source cannot be read, or installing the engine
0080| fails. The failure message names the required minimum, the engine version found
0081| or offered, and what you can do next. A successful run states the engine version
0082| in place and how it was obtained: installed, kept or replaced.
0083| 
0084| Running the same documented install again therefore replaces the client and
0085| compares the engine already in place with the engine that run would provide: the
0086| engine is installed when it is missing or strictly older, and an equal or newer
0087| engine is left exactly as it is, so an existing newer engine is never taken
0088| backwards.
0089| 
0090| ### Engine version
0091| 
0092| The one minimum supported engine version is 0.1.0: the client accepts an engine
0093| at that version or newer and refuses engine-backed work when the engine it finds
0094| is older. A reader whose engine is missing or too old sees a message that says
0095| what is wrong and what to run instead of a bare not-found error:
0096| 
0097| - **No engine.** The client reports that it requires the `forgel` engine, at
0098|   the minimum supported engine version of 0.1.0 or newer, and that it could not
0099|   be started. It points at the install that supplies one; the combined install
0100|   above brings an engine at that minimum or newer.
0101| - **Too old.** The client reports that it requires engine version 0.1.0 or
0102|   newer while the engine it found reports its own lower version, so the version
0103|   found and the 0.1.0 minimum are both named, and it points at the upgrade:
0104|   running the combined install above again.
0105| 
0106| Asking the client about itself does not need an engine. Its version output,
0107| `forgel-code --version`, and its machine-readable form,
0108| `forgel-code --version --json`, which carries the client's version next to the
0109| minimum supported engine version, answer with no engine installed and without
0110| contacting the network; so does the diagnostic answer, `forgel-code --help`.
0111| Every command that needs the engine fails with the message above while no engine
0112| at 0.1.0 or newer is present.
0113| 
0114| ### The engine on its own
0115| 
0116| The engine installs on its own through its own installer, `forgel-install` —
0117| one action, and the path for a reader who wants the engine without the client or
0118| who already has the client:
0119| 
0120| ```sh
0121| forgel-install --source https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel --install <version>
0122| ```
0123| 
0124| That installs the engine version named in `<version>`, which is one at the
0125| minimum supported engine version, 0.1.0, or newer. `forgel-install --source
0126| <source> --available-version` prints which engine version a source provides
0127| without installing anything. The source and the installer command are
0128| configuration, described under **Engine source** below.
0129| 
0130| ### Engine source
0131| 
0132| The engine source the run resolves against is configuration with a default, and
0133| either variable can point it elsewhere.
0134| 
0135| | Variable | Effect |
0136| | --- | --- |

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command, and that command installs the `forgel`
0015| engine the client runs as well: one action leaves a working client-and-engine
0016| pair, with no second program to find, install or version-match. Running it
0017| exactly as shown needs no option, flag or follow-up step. It needs Python 3.9 or
0018| newer with the `pip` module it ships.
0019| 
0020| ```sh
0021| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0022| ```
0023| 
0024| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0025| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0026| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0027| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0028| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0029| 
0030| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0031| | --- | --- |
0032| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0033| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0034| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0035| 
0036| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0037| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0038| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0039| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0040| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0041| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0042| 
0043| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0044| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0045| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0046| `export PATH=...` line.
0047| 
0048| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0049| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0050| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0051| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0052| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0053| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0054| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0055| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0056| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0057| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0058| was.

0002| 
0003| All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
0004|

0007| 
0008| ## [Unreleased]
0009| 
0010| ### Added
0011| 
0012| - Document the paired install and the supported engine range in the client's user documentation — the front page now presents one default install action that brings the engine and the client in as one pair with no option or follow-up step, and no longer asks the reader to obtain an engine before installing the client. The engine's standalone install is documented as its own separate path for a reader who wants the engine alone or already has the client, and the minimum supported engine version is stated as one concrete version that an older engine is refused against. The page describes the message a user sees when no engine is found and when the engine is too old, each naming what is wrong, the version involved and the install or upgrade to run, and states that the client's version and diagnostic answers still work without an engine. It states the repeat-install behaviour: the engine is installed only when it is missing or strictly older, and an equal or newer engine is left exactly as it is, so it is never taken backwards.
0013| 
0014| - Report the client version and the minimum supported engine version together — `forgel-code --version --json` prints one machine-readable object with the client's own version and the engine version the client supports at minimum, and it answers on a machine where no engine is installed and without contacting the network. Both values come from the client's declaration and never from an installed engine, and the human-readable `forgel-code --version` output is unchanged.
0015| 
0016| - Install the client and a supported engine in one run — the default installation no longer stops at the client. It asks the configured engine source which version it offers, without changing anything, reads the version of an engine already in place, and then decides: an absent engine is obtained, a present engine at or above the client's declared minimum is kept when the offered version is not strictly newer, and a strictly newer offered engine replaces it. An engine at or below the version in place is never installed. The finished state always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version, otherwise the run fails with a message naming the required minimum, the version found or offered, and the action that supplies a satisfying engine. A successful run reports the engine version in place and whether it was installed, kept or replaced. The engine source and the engine's own installer are documented configuration with defaults, `--client-only` installs the client alone without querying or touching any engine, leaving the shell profile unchanged still performs the engine part, removing the client leaves the engine in place, and repeating the default run changes no engine that needs no change. The README documents the combined installation, the client-only installation and the engine source.
0017| 
0018| - Open an interactive session when the client starts with no arguments — `forgel-code` now shows a prompt and stays open instead of printing usage text. A sentence typed at the prompt is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session shows the selected project and lets the owner switch it without leaving, shows a plan as its ordered tasks with their states and a new task with its title and state, and re-reads the task and release state from the engine on its own so progress appears without asking for a status. Accepting a task, sending it back with remarks, retrying a failed task, pausing and resuming work are asked for in plain language, an ambiguous or unmatched request gets a clarification and performs nothing, a failure shows the reason and the next possible step while the session stays usable, and replies follow the language of the owner's message. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit separate actions that a sentence never triggers, key material never reaches the screen, and leaving — or the end of the input — ends the session at once. The session adds no capability: every answer and every piece of state still comes from the engine, and every one-shot usage keeps its previous output, exit status and `--json` form.
0019| 
0020| ### Changed
0021| 
0022| - Speed up the suite without weakening a test — the expensive duplicated work is gone instead of a scenario: one read-only checkout copy and one prepared installation per scenario group are shared by the tests that only read them, and the bounded-check cases configure a limit below the product default.
0023| - Remove every statement of a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound from the documentation — the README `## Tests` section still says that one documented command runs the whole suite, that the installer situations are covered by a real installation into a throwaway home location with a real detected login shell, and that a run from a source checkout needs only the Python standard library and no network access, but it no longer promises how long such a run takes.
0024| 
0025| ### Removed
0026| 
0027| - Remove the automated check that read the installation instructions — no check reads a documentation file any more, because documentation is text and is accepted or returned by a person reading it. The check and the data it kept to reproduce the installation commands are gone in full, no automated check of documentation text replaces them, and every other check stays in place. The guard that used to fail the suite when a documented install, update or uninstall command carried an older tag is gone with it, so the three commands stay tied together by review of their text rather than by a check.

0030| 
0031| - Read an installed engine's version from the report the engine actually answers — the combined installation asked an engine already in place in an undocumented form and read a part its documented answer does not carry, so a healthy supported engine was treated as missing or unreadable and an offered version equal to or older than it could be installed over it. The run now asks the engine the way the client does and reads its answer the way the client does: a supported engine that reports its version is recognized at exactly the version it reports and kept with no engine installed when the offered version is not strictly newer, a strictly newer offered version still replaces it, repeating the default run leaves the same engine and one client installation, and a version that cannot be ordered is still below the minimum and replaced by a supported offered version.
0032| - Refuse a free-text request to create or change key material, to change configuration and to create or scaffold a project in English and in Russian, including their bare wording — a sentence that names a key without any credential term, the configuration without the word `configuration`, or a project that is scaffolded rather than created is now recognised, refused in the session and never forwarded to the engine, and the refusal states that the action needs the explicit operation and names the client's own `forgel-code` command to use. Ordinary conversation that merely mentions a key, the configuration or a project still reaches the engine unchanged, and every refusal that already existed keeps its wording.
0033| - Mask the value of the French password label when it is written with underscores or hyphens — the label is now recognised as a secret label in its joined spellings as well as its spaced one, in any letter case, so an engine reply or error that carries it next to a value is redacted before display and before retention. Every value form already handled for the spaced label is covered, a joined label without an adjacent value leaves the message unchanged, and every other supported label in every language redacts exactly as before.
0034| - Refuse sensitive explicit actions phrased in French and Spanish as well as in English and Russian — a free-text request to create a project, to set or define a credential such as a password, a token or a key, or to change configuration or settings is recognised in all four languages the session speaks, in either word order, in ordinary inflections and with or without diacritics. The refusal-and-redirect answer speaks the language of the message, states that such an action is never carried out from a sentence, and then points at the client's own explicit command `forgel-code` together with the action it performs — creating a project, setting or defining a password, a token or a key, or changing the configuration — in the same style as the English and Russian refusals. Nothing of the refused request is sent onward, ordinary French and Spanish conversation still reaches the engine unchanged, and English and Russian results stay exactly as they were.
0035| - Mask the credential of a label followed by an ordinary descriptor word — a secret label followed by a word such as `value`, `field` or `string` used to hide that descriptor and leave the credential itself on screen and in the retained state; the descriptor now stays readable and the value, including the one behind a copula or a separator, is replaced by the existing masking placeholder. Sentences that only mention a secret word are still shown unchanged.
0036| - Remove the PATH block from the profile named by `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` — `--uninstall` again cleans the marked block out of the profile the override variable names, in addition to the six standard profile files, so a block left by a completed install or by an install that failed its fresh-shell check no longer survives.
0037| - Point the README install, update and uninstall commands at the current `v0.2.0` release installer — the documented commands no longer fetch the stale install script, and all three name one and the same install-script URL.
